summary: Built 1958 at Fort Klamath, airlifted to Sugarpine Mountain in 1970; staffed each summer, drive-up, still standing; NHLR-registered 2022.

facts.design: 20-foot open steel X-brace tower with a 13x13 CL-100 cab

access.note: Drive-up summit on the Winema National Forest; the statewide standing-lookout list marks it accessible to the public.

visit.trail_note: A 2025 visitor reported an easy drive to the summit.

events.note: Summit first used as a camp lookout site, in the 1930s (no exact year given).
Built at Fort Klamath as a 20-foot open steel tower with a 13x13 cab. This is the date for the structure at its original site.
32 hours of road and lookout site construction at Sugarpine Mountain.
Tower and cab airlifted from Fort Klamath to the Sugarpine Mountain summit.
Herald and News reported a lookout might be stationed by mid-May if dry weather continued.
Winema National Forest let the fire-watch job by contract for the first time; before, lookout personnel were hired.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1641 on July 6, 2022.
Staffed in summer at the June 2025 visit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the structure to 1958 at Fort Klamath; firelookout.com says the summit was first used as a camp lookout in the 1930s and that the first permanent structure arrived in 1970. The story gives both dates and treats 1970 as the date the tower reached the summit.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1958 build date is for the structure at Fort Klamath, not on Sugarpine; the summit's lookout dates from the 1970 airlift, so the 1958 event is annotated accordingly. No notable fires appear in any source read. No rental listing was found in the two searches run, so the story says nothing about rentals. Staffing is from the 2025 visit and undated firelookout.com text; the 1983 contract is from a Herald and News item quoted on oregonlookouts.weebly.com.
